headline: Energy Leads a Lopsided Session as Middle East Tensions Rattle Broader Markets
body_html:
Thursday's midday tape tells a stark story: sellers have the upper hand across most of the market, with decliners outpacing advancers 384 to 164 in our 550-name universe. The dominant theme is geopolitical anxiety, as escalating tensions in the Middle East — including warnings exchanged between Israel and Turkey over Syria and an ongoing U.S.-Iran military impasse — are driving commodity-linked names higher while weighing on growth and consumer sectors.

Energy is the clear session leader, advancing 1.37%, with Murphy Oil adding 4.22% mid-session. Semiconductors are clinging to modest gains of 0.37%, the only other sector in positive territory. On the other end of the ledger, Homebuilders are the worst performers, off 1.53%, followed by Consumer stocks sliding 1.24% and Software retreating 1.18%. Materials are also under pressure, down 0.98%, as risk appetite narrows sharply.

The standout mover of the session belongs to ScanSource, surging 26.41% — a magnitude that suggests a company-specific catalyst rather than macro drift. CF Industries is rising 7.63%, benefiting from agricultural-chemical tailwinds. Into the close, watch whether crude-linked names can sustain their bid as Hormuz shipping data remains steady despite the broader war stalemate.

briefs.headline: ScanSource Rockets Higher on Apparent Catalyst
briefs.body: Tech-distribution firm ScanSource is the session's undisputed standout, surging 26.41% mid-session — a move of an order of magnitude that points to a company-specific development rather than sector momentum. No broader Tech-Distribution peers are registering comparable moves, underscoring the idiosyncratic nature of the jump. Traders will be watching for any incremental disclosure into the close.

briefs.headline: Crude Climbs to Three-Week High as Iran Standoff Lingers
briefs.body: Oil prices have reached their highest level in over three weeks as markets price in sustained Middle East supply risk. A U.S.-Iran military stalemate, combined with warnings from Washington of economic consequences for nations backing Tehran, is keeping the risk premium elevated. Murphy Oil gained 4.22%, reflecting the direct uplift to upstream producers from firmer crude.

briefs.headline: China's Appetite for Russian Crude Squeezes India's Refiners
briefs.body: China has stepped up purchases of Russian crude, reducing the supply available to Indian refiners who had grown reliant on discounted barrels. The shift tightens the competitive landscape for Asian refining margins and adds another variable to a global oil market already strained by Middle East uncertainty. Energy-sector investors are closely monitoring regional crude flow data.

briefs.headline: CF Industries and Corteva Lead Agriculture Names Higher
briefs.body: Fertilizer producer CF Industries jumped 7.63% while crop-science company Corteva advanced 4.05%, making agriculture-linked equities a bright spot in an otherwise defensive session. The gains align with broader commodity strength as geopolitical disruptions elevate input-price expectations. Both names rank among Thursday's top six gainers across the entire universe.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Retreats as MongoDB Slides
briefs.body: The Software sector is down 1.18% at midday, with database platform MongoDB among the steeper individual decliners, off 4.52%. The weakness reflects a broader rotation away from high-multiple growth names as risk sentiment sours. Logitech, a Tech-Peripherals name, is also sliding 4.29%, suggesting the pressure extends across technology sub-segments beyond pure software.

briefs.headline: Consumer and Homebuilder Stocks Bear the Brunt of Selling
briefs.body: Consumer names are off 1.24% and Homebuilders are the session's worst-performing sector at -1.53%, as rate-sensitive and discretionary stocks absorb the bulk of today's selling pressure. Carter's dropped 4.50% and Floor & Decor fell 3.93%, illustrating the breadth of weakness in spending-dependent segments. Analysts note that an elevated geopolitical risk backdrop tends to compress consumer confidence expectations.
